## \> *Evolution of spatial inequalities in mortality across 90 French territorial units since 1806. We identify a period from 1881 to 1980 when inequalities rapidly shrank while life expectancy rose. The geography of mortality also changed radically: from a North-west/South-east line in the 19th century to a North-only concentration today, with Paris and Lyon enjoying an urban advantage.*
